$comment: Edge proxy (Caddy) configuration. This file is committed — put SECRETS in env/vault, never here. See edge/README.md.
$enabled: Master switch. While false, deploy-edge.sh refuses to ship anything — generate/preflight/reconcile still work (reconcile stays dry-run).
$proxyMode: 'caddy' = the managed container this module deploys. 'dsm' = keep Synology's (or any other hand-managed) reverse proxy: Caddyfile generation and deploy stand down, but DNS reconciliation, DDNS, and preflight verification all still run — preflight then connects to each domain's public endpoint (port 443) and asserts health + WebSocket upgrades against YOUR proxy.
$dnsProvider: DEFAULT provider: any module in edge/dns/ ('porkbun', 'cloudflare', 'none', ...). 'none' disables DNS automation and DNS-01 certs — Caddy then uses HTTP-01, which requires public port 80. Add a provider by dropping a module in edge/dns/ that implements the interface in edge/dns/provider.js. Set YOUR provider in the registry's "edge" block, not here — this file is committed and shared by every deploy-kit user.
$zoneProviders: Per-zone provider overrides for domains at OTHER registrars, e.g. { "clankerbox.com": "cloudflare" }. Reconciliation, DDNS, and DNS-01 cert challenges all use the zone's own provider; the Caddy image compiles every needed plugin.
$tlsMode: 'internal' = Caddy's self-signed CA (pre-cutover testing, preflight uses --insecure). 'auto' = real ACME certs; uses the DNS-01 challenge when dnsProvider != 'none' (works BEFORE the router flip — no inbound traffic needed).
$ports: Host ports the Caddy container publishes on the NAS. At cutover the router forwards public 80→18080 and 443→18443. DSM keeps its own 80/443 untouched (instant rollback).
$publicIp: 'auto' = dynamic connection: detect the egress IP each run and DDNS repoints records when it drifts (schedule ddns-update.js). An explicit IP = static connection: the declared value is the source of truth — records are enforced to it, DDNS scheduling becomes optional insurance, and a loud warning fires if the actual egress IP ever disagrees with the declaration.
$anchorRecord: Single A record the reconciler points at the current public IP (e.g. "home.example.com"); every other managed hostname becomes CNAME/ALIAS → anchor. An ISP IP change is then one ddns-update call. Per-deployment — set it in the registry's "edge" block.
$zoneOverrides: Map domain → DNS zone for cases the default 'last two labels' heuristic gets wrong (e.g. "foo.co.uk": "foo.co.uk").
$extraSites: Routes for things NOT in the registry (DSM apps etc.): [{ "domain": "nas.rod.dev", "upstream": "192.168.86.2:5001" }]
$wsChecks: Preflight asserts a real WebSocket 101 upgrade through the proxy for these — the exact failure class a stripping reverse proxy silently causes. Per-deployment (set in the registry's "edge" block): [{ "domain": "api.chat.example.com", "path": "/ws" }]
